`main` shall execute the entire pipeline on the thread on which it was entered, creating no additional thread.
`main` shall invoke `graph_write_dot` when, and only when, `graph_dot_warranted` returns true.

`main` shall open the output destination named by the options, or use standard output when none was named, and shall emit a diagnostic and return 2 when that destination cannot be opened or cannot be written, rather than reporting a truncated report as success.

trace.name: Diagnostics on stderr, Results on stdout

llr.text: `main` shall record a file skipped for want of a usable language module in the report's skipped-file list and emit a diagnostic naming it, and shall not count the skip as a per-file failure.
`main` shall release every resource it acquired before returning, on the success path and on every error path alike, so that a completed run leaves no allocation, mapping, or handle outstanding.

function.title: `cli_parse` ([src/cli.c](../src/cli.c))
function.name: cli_parse
function.intro: Command-line parsing and validation. `cli_parse` is the sole reader of `argv` and the sole source of user-supplied configuration.

llr.text: `cli_parse` shall accept one or more target arguments in any combination of file and directory names, and shall reject an invocation supplying none.
`cli_parse` shall accept a report format selection of `table`, `csv`, `xml`, or `md`, defaulting to `table` when none is supplied.

`cli_parse` shall accept `--entry` repeatedly, accumulating one entry-point symbol per occurrence, and shall never infer an entry point from any other source. The symbols are borrowed from `argv`; only the array holding them is owned.
`cli_parse` shall accept an output file path, and shall record standard output as the destination when none is supplied.
`cli_parse` shall accept a cyclomatic-complexity threshold and shall default it to 15 when none is supplied.
`cli_parse` shall accept a bottleneck coupling threshold and shall default it to 5 when none is supplied.
`cli_parse` shall enable `.dot` call-tree generation by default and shall disable it when the corresponding option is supplied.
`cli_parse` shall accept a GraphML export request as a flag taking no path argument.
`cli_parse` shall accept zero or more entry-point symbol declarations, and shall leave the entry-point set empty when none is supplied.
`cli_parse` shall accept custom rule declarations that name both a language and a path, and shall reject a declaration naming only a path.

`cli_parse` shall accept a regeneration-mode input path. In regeneration mode the report format shall default to Markdown rather than to the table format, and only a format *explicitly* selected and other than Markdown shall be rejected.

trace.name: No Companion Artefacts From a Saved Record

llr.text: `cli_parse` shall accept a complexity threshold in regeneration mode independently of any threshold recorded in the input file, defaulting to 15.
`cli_parse` shall report a usage error for an unrecognised option, for a missing or malformed argument to an option requiring one, and for a missing target.
`cli_parse` shall report a help request when the help option is supplied, without validating any other argument.

trace.name: Help Request Is Not an Error

llr.text: `cli_parse` shall derive the options structure solely from the arguments passed to it, opening no file in the working directory, the analysis target, or any ancestor of either.
`cli_parse` shall reject a numeric option argument that is not a plain decimal number consumed in its entirety, rather than accepting the prefix that a permissive conversion would read from it.
`cli_parse` shall reject a target given alongside a regeneration-mode input path, since the record is the input and a target would name a second source for one report.

`cli_parse` shall reject as a usage error a command line that combines regeneration mode with an explicit request for a companion artefact, since a saved record does not carry the graph from which either could be produced.

trace.name: No Companion Artefacts From a Saved Record

llr.text: `cli_usage` shall write a summary naming every accepted option, its argument if any, and its default value.

trace.name: Help Request Is Not an Error

llr.text: `cli_usage` shall write to the stream it is given, so that a help request may be directed to standard output and a usage error to standard error.

trace.name: Help Request Is Not an Error
Diagnostics on stderr, Results on stdout

llr.text: `parse_stratum` shall parse a declaration naming an architectural layer and the component patterns assigned to it.
`parse_stratum` shall record the declared ordinal of each layer, so that the permitted direction of dependency between layers is determined.
`parse_stratum` shall report a usage error for a declaration that cannot be parsed, rather than silently ignoring it.
`parse_scope` shall parse a declaration naming an execution scope and the components belonging to it.
`parse_scope` shall report a usage error for a declaration that cannot be parsed.

function.title: `discover_targets` ([src/discover.c](../src/discover.c))
function.name: discover_targets
function.intro: Target validation, classification, and file discovery. Produces the de-duplicated, stably ordered list every later stage consumes.

llr.text: `discover_targets` shall validate every target argument with `stat(2)` before walking any of them.

`discover_targets` shall emit a diagnostic naming the offending target and return non-zero, without producing any file list, when a target does not exist, cannot be opened or read, or is neither a regular file nor a directory.

`discover_targets` shall classify each validated target independently of every other, so that files and directories may be intermixed on one command line, and a directory target shall denote the same set of files whichever discovery route it takes.

trace.name: Repository Enumeration Scoped to the Target

llr.text: `discover_targets` shall append a target that is a regular file directly to the file list, performing no directory traversal for it.

`discover_targets` shall offer each directory target to `git_repository_open_ext`, which searches the target directory and then its ancestors, and shall route the target to `walk_git_tree` only when a repository is found *and* that repository tracks the target directory. In every other case — no repository, or a repository that does not track the target — it shall route the target to `walk_filesystem`.
`discover_targets` shall resolve a target that is a symbolic link, since `stat(2)` follows links and a link named explicitly identifies its referent.
`discover_targets` shall canonicalise every accumulated path and shall retain exactly one entry per canonical path, so that a file reached through more than one target is analysed once.
`discover_targets` shall sort the completed file list into a defined order that does not depend on the enumeration order of the filesystem or of the repository.

`discover_targets` shall record, for each directory target, whether it was enumerated from a repository or traversed from the filesystem, and shall pass that record forward for reporting. Each record shall name the target's canonical absolute path, as every other path in the report does, and shall hold one record per directory: two spellings of one directory reach the same route by definition, so a second record would report a run over two targets that was a run over one. Each record shall own a copy of the target it names rather than aliasing the caller's string. Aliasing would happen to work on the analysis path, where targets are `argv` entries that outlive the run, and would fail on the regeneration path, where they are parsed out of a record and released — the kind of difference that shows up as a corrupted Discovery section in one mode only.
`discover_targets` shall emit a diagnostic and record a per-file failure for a subdirectory that cannot be read, and shall continue the traversal.

`walk_git_tree` shall resolve the tree at `HEAD` and enumerate only those blobs whose repository-relative path lies at or beneath the target directory, so that a subdirectory target does not draw in the rest of the repository.

trace.name: Repository Enumeration Scoped to the Target

llr.text: `walk_git_tree` shall report the repository inapplicable when it tracks nothing at or beneath the target directory, so that the caller falls back to filesystem traversal rather than returning an empty file list. Applicability shall be determined from the tree walk itself rather than by a separate query made beforehand: two traversals can disagree, and a disagreement between them would present as an empty report rather than as an error. It shall be determined from what the repository *tracks* and not from what survived the exclusion filters, since a tracked directory holding only excluded files is still tracked — judging it otherwise would fall back to the filesystem and analyse the untracked files this route exists to exclude. An applicable repository may therefore yield no files at all.
`walk_git_tree` shall include only files tracked at `HEAD`, so that ignored and untracked paths are excluded without a separate exclusion list.
`walk_git_tree` shall exclude every blob reported as binary.
`walk_filesystem` shall traverse the directory tree recursively, appending each regular file that survives filtering.
`walk_filesystem` shall exclude hidden entries — files as well as directories — from the traversal, a hidden entry being one whose name begins with a period.
`walk_filesystem` shall exclude files whose extension appears in the binary-extension list.

`render_summary` shall traverse the report model in a single shared order for both the table and Markdown renderers, so that the two present the same tiers.
`format_csv` shall emit one record per function over the complete dataset, unfiltered by the complexity threshold.
`format_csv` shall emit per-function metrics only, excluding the architectural findings.
`write_field` shall quote and escape every field whose value contains a comma, a double-quote character, or a line break, in accordance with RFC 4180.
Every emitted CSV field shall pass through `write_field`, so that a value such as a template signature containing a comma cannot corrupt the record structure.
`xml_write_report` shall emit the complete dataset of a run, unfiltered by the complexity threshold.
`xml_write_report` shall emit every element any report may present: the project totals, the per-file totals, the per-function detail, the architectural findings, and any custom-rule matches.
`xml_write_report` shall emit a format-version identifier in the document root.

`xml_write_report` shall omit an element it has nothing to record rather than emit it empty, and the format-version identifier shall be incremented for a removal or a change of meaning and not for an addition, so that a record written by a later build remains readable by an earlier one of the same version.

`xml_write_report` shall write each target's discovery route to the record. A record that omitted it would regenerate into a report with an empty Discovery section — well-formed, carrying every measurement, and not the same report — which is the one thing HLR-056 forbids.

`xml_write_report` shall write the unresolved-call count to the record, and `xml_read_report` shall restore it. It is a measurement of the run like any other and cannot be recomputed later: regeneration has no graph, and no source from which to build one.

`xml_write_report` shall write the call-tree measurements to the record — every function's fan-out, every recursive cycle's members, the depth and its state, and the deepest chain in order — and `xml_read_report` shall restore them. None can be recomputed from a record: regeneration has no graph, and no source from which to build one.
`xml_write_report` shall emit well-formed XML.
`write_escaped` shall escape every character carrying structural meaning in XML, so that an identifier or path containing such a character cannot render the document unparseable.
Every emitted XML element body and attribute value shall pass through `write_escaped`.
`xml_read_report` shall reconstruct a report model from a previously written record without parsing or re-analysing any source file.
`xml_read_report` shall parse the record with a streaming parser, materialising no document tree.
`xml_read_report` shall reject, with a diagnostic and a non-zero exit status, an input that is not well-formed XML.
`xml_read_report` shall reject an input that does not match `elc`'s own output structure.
`xml_read_report` shall reject an input whose format-version identifier this build does not support, naming the version found.

`xml_read_report` shall reconstruct only the measurements a record carries and shall derive every reported total, breakdown, callout, ordering, and threshold listing with the same code that derives them for a live run, so that a regenerated report cannot differ from a direct one by way of a second implementation.

`xml_read_report` shall treat an attribute that should be numeric and is not as a malformed record rather than as a zero, since a record accepted on those terms renders cleanly and reports the wrong figures.

`xml_read_report` shall rebuild the discovery routes from the record and hand them to `report_assemble`, so that a regenerated report presents the same Discovery section as the run that produced the record. A route element lacking either its target or its route, or naming a route this build does not recognise, shall be rejected as a malformed record rather than defaulted: a defaulted route is not an unknown answer but a confident wrong one, in the section whose whole purpose is explaining a surprising file set.
`xml_read_report` shall attempt no best-effort partial conversion of a rejected input.
`xml_read_report` shall apply the complexity threshold supplied at conversion time, independently of any threshold in force when the record was written.
The reconstructed model shall render byte-identically to the report a direct analysis would have produced at the same threshold.
`graph_dot_warranted` shall return true by default, and false when the user has disabled `.dot` generation.
`graph_dot_warranted` shall return false whenever the report is written to standard output, whether or not generation was disabled.
`graph_dot_warranted` shall return false in regeneration mode, since a saved record does not carry the graph.

trace.name: No Companion Artefacts From a Saved Record

llr.text: `graph_write_dot` shall emit the call tree in Graphviz DOT format.
`graph_write_dot` shall require no library dependency and shall not invoke Graphviz.
`graph_write_dot` shall derive its filename from the report's output path by extension substitution, accepting no output path of its own.
`graph_write_dot` shall emit nodes in ascending stable node-identifier order and each node's adjacency in ascending target order, so that no internal enumeration order reaches the output.
`graph_write_dot` shall emit a diagnostic and record a failure, while leaving the primary report written, when the companion file cannot be created.

`node_style` shall annotate nodes exceeding the coupling and fan-out thresholds, the functions forming the deepest call chain, the members of each dependency and recursive cycle, unreachable functions, and functions participating in a hidden channel.
`node_style` shall emit annotations as attributes a renderer may ignore while still producing a valid call tree.
`graph_write_graphml` shall export the graph in the GraphML serialisation schema so that it may be ingested by other tools.
`graph_write_graphml` shall run only when explicitly requested, being disabled by default.
`graph_write_graphml` shall derive its filename from the report's output path, and shall produce no file when the report is written to standard output.
`graph_write_graphml` shall emit well-formed XML with every structurally significant character escaped.

function.title: Build and Link Configuration ([Makefile](../Makefile))
function.name: build_configuration
function.intro: Requirements satisfied by the build rather than by any single function. Verified against the produced binary rather than at runtime.

llr.text: The build shall link `elc` against no interpreter and no virtual machine, and the produced binary shall require none at execution.
`elc` shall perform no network access at any point during execution, and shall produce identical results when run without network availability.
The build shall require no code generation step.

The build shall select the third-party libraries `elc` links against, any of which may be substituted for another satisfying the same role, save for the parsing library whose query language and grammar format are a product contract.

The build shall link an established graph library providing cycle detection, topological ordering, reachability, and centrality, rather than hand-implemented equivalents. Every optional feature of that library that would alter `elc`'s link line shall be pinned explicitly rather than left to the library's configure-time detection: a default of "use it if it is installed" makes the binary a function of the build machine, which the instrumented dependency allowlist — a fixed list — cannot express.

trace.name: Graph Algorithms From an Established Library

llr.text: The build shall configure the graph library so that it does not itself introduce a dependency on an unmaintained XML library.

trace.name: Graph Algorithms From an Established Library

llr.text: The build shall deliver runtime language support for C, C++, Rust, Python, and Ada, each as a grammar and its query files under the runtime location, requiring no change to any source module of the executable.
The documented set of required query files and capture names shall be published with the delivered runtime, so that a third party may add a language against it.

trace.name: Language Module Interface Is a Stable Contract

llr.text: The build shall support link-time symbol interception for the unit level, so that a dependency can be replaced by a test without a seam being carried in `src/`. A toolchain that cannot provide it cannot run the unit suite and is unsupported rather than worked around.

trace.name: Graph Algorithms From an Established Library

llr.text: The build shall apply the language standard, the warning set, and the header-dependency generation it requires in a way that a caller-supplied `CFLAGS` cannot displace, so that a build invoked with an added flag is compiled under the same rules as one invoked with none.

The build shall produce each delivered language grammar from a pinned upstream release, compiling the generated parser that release publishes, so that no code-generation step is required at build time and the version delivered is a recorded decision rather than whatever was current.

The build shall carry its usage summary as a marked comment block in the makefile's own header and shall print that block for the help target, so that one text serves a reader who opens the file and a reader who runs it, and shall fail its own test suite when that block and the set of declared targets disagree.

The delivered source shall avoid the C constructs the delivered grammar cannot parse — a multi-token type argument to a variadic accessor, and a macro standing between a function's return type and its name — so that `elc` can analyse its own source without a per-file failure.

The build shall take the upstream owner and the archive reference of each grammar as parameters rather than as constants, so that a grammar hosted outside the parsing library's own organisation, or one whose upstream cuts no releases and must be pinned by commit, is added as data without a change to any source module.

The build shall locate a grammar's external scanner at the time the compile command runs rather than when the rule is expanded, since a grammar linked without the scanner it requires fails at load rather than at build.

The build shall report, for each delivered grammar, the reference it is pinned to and the reference upstream carries now, so that a pin which is immutable is not thereby invisible when it falls behind.
The build shall provide a configuration instrumented with AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer, with leak detection enabled, under which the whole test suite can be re-run.

function.title: User Documentation ([doc/elc.1](../doc/elc.1), [doc/User_Manual.md](../doc/User_Manual.md))
function.name: user_documentation
function.intro: Requirements met by the delivered documentation rather than by any function. Verified against the built binary and the install tree, in the manner of the build-configuration group.

llr.text: A `man` page for `elc` shall be delivered in section-1 roff form, and shall render without diagnostic under a standard man-page formatter.

trace.name: User Manual and Man Page Delivered

llr.text: A user manual shall be delivered describing every capability with at least one worked example per output format and per analysis family.

trace.name: User Manual and Man Page Delivered

llr.text: The install target shall place the man page into the section-1 manual path and the user manual alongside the delivered runtime, both under the staging root when one is given.

trace.name: User Manual and Man Page Delivered

llr.text: Every option appearing in `elc`'s usage summary shall appear in both the man page and the user manual, and every option documented in either shall be accepted by `elc`; the usage summary is the reference against which both are checked.
Every report format, companion artefact, and category of reported finding shall be described in both documents.
A change altering an option, a format, an artefact, or a finding category shall update both documents within the same change, and shall be treated as incomplete otherwise.

trace.name: Documentation Updated With the Behaviour It Describes

test.name: wrap_passes_through_when_not_armed
test.purpose: An unarmed link-time wrapper delegates to the real implementation, so wrapping does not perturb tests that do not use it.

test.name: wrap_intercepts_when_armed
test.purpose: An armed wrapper intercepts the call, proving the mechanism by which later phases provoke allocation failure.

test.name: help_short_option_reports_help
test.purpose: `-h` is reported as a help request rather than parsed as an ordinary option.

test.name: help_long_option_reports_help
test.purpose: `--help` is reported as a help request.

test.name: unrecognised_option_is_a_usage_error
test.purpose: An unrecognised option is rejected as a usage error.

test.name: missing_target_is_a_usage_error
test.purpose: An invocation with no target is rejected as a usage error.

test.name: single_target_is_collected
test.purpose: A single target argument is collected into the options structure.

test.name: several_targets_are_collected_in_order
test.purpose: Several targets are collected in argument order, files and directories intermixed.

test.name: help_takes_precedence_over_a_target
test.purpose: A help request is reported without validating the remaining arguments.

test.name: mode_defaults_to_analyse
test.purpose: The run mode defaults to analysis when no mode-selecting option is given.

test.name: the_output_destination_defaults_to_standard_output
test.purpose: A null output path records standard output as the destination when none was supplied.

test.name: an_output_path_is_collected
test.purpose: An output file path is collected into the options, and its argument is not mistaken for a target.

test.name: the_short_output_option_behaves_as_the_long_one
test.purpose: The short form of the redirection option is parsed as the long form is.

test.name: an_output_option_without_its_argument_is_a_usage_error
test.purpose: An option requiring an argument and given none is a usage error.

test.name: the_complexity_threshold_defaults_to_fifteen
test.purpose: The threshold defaults to the documented value when none is supplied.

test.name: a_complexity_threshold_is_collected
test.purpose: A threshold given as a long option is collected, and its argument is not mistaken for a target.

test.name: the_short_threshold_option_behaves_as_the_long_one
test.purpose: The short form is parsed as the long form is.

test.name: a_threshold_of_zero_is_accepted
test.purpose: Zero lists every function, which is a legitimate request and must not be read as absent.

test.name: a_malformed_threshold_is_a_usage_error
test.purpose: A sign, a trailing tail, leading whitespace, an empty string, and a hexadecimal literal are each rejected — every one of which a permissive conversion would accept, silently yielding a threshold the user did not write.

test.name: options_free_is_safe_on_null
test.purpose: Releasing a null options structure does not fault, so teardown is safe on every path.

test.name: the_environment_variable_names_the_runtime_location
test.purpose: The environment variable names the runtime location, and wins over the path adjacent to the executable — which for a unit binary does not exist at all.

test.name: an_absent_runtime_location_is_fatal
test.purpose: A runtime location that does not exist ends the run: no analysis is possible without one.

test.name: a_runtime_location_that_is_a_file_is_fatal
test.purpose: A runtime location that is a regular file is the same unusable state as a missing one, and is treated the same way.

test.name: an_extension_map_naming_no_language_is_fatal
test.purpose: An extension map naming no language leaves nothing that can be routed to a module, which is the state HLR-036 calls fatal.

test.name: the_extension_map_is_runtime_data
test.purpose: Pointing an unrelated extension at a language resolves, and an extension the data does not name does not — so the mapping is read from runtime data rather than compiled in.

test.name: the_extension_map_tolerates_comments_and_bare_extensions
test.purpose: Comments and blank lines are not entries, an extension written without its leading period still matches, and matching ignores case.

test.name: a_module_is_loaded_on_first_use_of_its_extension
test.purpose: A file's language comes from its extension alone, and first use loads the grammar and compiles all six queries.

test.name: a_language_is_loaded_at_most_once
test.purpose: A second lookup returns the cached module, so a language is loaded at most once per run and a mixed-language target needs one pass.

test.name: an_unmapped_extension_yields_no_module
test.purpose: An extension the map does not name, and a file name with no extension at all, both yield no module — so the caller skips rather than fails.

test.name: an_absent_grammar_makes_the_language_unusable
test.purpose: A module whose grammar is missing is excluded rather than fatal, and opening the registry does not load any grammar up front.

test.name: a_missing_query_file_makes_the_language_unusable
test.purpose: A module omitting one of the six required query files is handled as unusable, not as undefined behaviour.

test.name: an_invalid_query_makes_the_language_unusable
test.purpose: A query file that will not compile makes its language unusable rather than crashing the run or being silently ignored.

test.name: an_unusable_language_is_not_retried
test.purpose: A language that failed to load is recorded once, so the diagnostic is emitted once rather than once per file that would have used it.

test.name: no_particular_language_is_required
test.purpose: The registry opens over whatever the runtime location holds and verifies no particular language up front.

test.name: close_is_safe_on_null_and_on_a_zeroed_registry
test.purpose: Teardown is safe on a null and on a never-opened registry, so every error path can release unconditionally.

test.name: physical_lines_are_counted
test.purpose: The physical line count comes from the mapped contents.

test.name: an_unterminated_final_line_counts
test.purpose: A trailing fragment with no terminating newline is a line the reader sees, and is counted as one.

test.name: a_zero_length_file_reports_zero_without_error
test.purpose: A file of zero length reports zero metrics without error, rather than being mapped — mmap of an empty file fails with EINVAL.

test.name: an_unreadable_file_is_a_failure_without_metrics
test.purpose: A file that cannot be read yields a failure and no metrics for the caller to release, so the run continues leak-free.

test.name: the_metrics_carry_the_path_and_language
test.purpose: The returned metrics carry the path measured and the language resolved for it.

test.name: a_function_is_reported_with_its_name_and_line_range
test.purpose: A function is reported with its name and its line range, the span beginning at the signature rather than at the body's opening brace.

test.name: a_nested_function_is_reported_in_its_own_right
test.purpose: A named function declared inside another is reported as a function of its own, with its own name and line range, rather than folded into its enclosing function.

test.name: a_prototype_is_not_a_function
test.purpose: A declaration without a body contributes no function: what counts as one is the query file's decision, and it supplies no body capture for a prototype.

test.name: a_function_name_outlives_the_mapping
test.purpose: A name is still readable after analyze_file returns, so it was copied out of the mapping rather than pointed into it.

test.name: a_file_that_fails_to_parse_is_a_failure
test.purpose: A file whose tree contains an error node is skipped whole and reported as a failure, rather than reported from a partially valid tree.

test.name: an_unmapped_extension_is_a_skip_not_a_failure
test.purpose: A file whose extension maps to no language is a skip, a distinct outcome from a failure, so the exit status stays 0.

test.name: spans_are_sorted_before_merging
test.purpose: Spans arriving out of order are sorted before anything is merged, and disjoint spans stay separate.

test.name: overlapping_spans_coalesce
test.purpose: Two spans that overlap become one covering both, so their shared lines are counted once.

test.name: a_nested_span_is_absorbed_not_counted_twice
test.purpose: A span wholly inside another is absorbed and contributes nothing of its own — the canonical case of a block comment carrying inline comment syntax, where subtracting per capture counts its lines twice.

test.name: a_shared_line_is_counted_once
test.purpose: A line shared by three comments is one line, however many spans touch it. Counting per span is what drives ELOC below zero.

test.name: coalescing_a_trailing_run_stays_in_bounds
test.purpose: Coalescing a run of spans that reaches the last element stops there. The bound is the whole of the requirement: without it the loop reads one past the final span whenever the trailing run is longer than one.

test.name: merging_an_empty_span_list_is_zero
test.purpose: A file with no comments merges to nothing without touching an empty array.

test.name: the_narrowest_enclosing_function_wins
test.purpose: A statement inside a nested function is attributed to that function rather than to the one enclosing it.

test.name: the_narrowest_wins_whatever_order_the_ranges_are_in
test.purpose: The answer does not depend on the order the ranges were discovered in — an implementation returning the first containing range would also break determinism.

test.name: an_offset_outside_every_function_has_no_owner
test.purpose: An offset outside every function belongs to none, so file-scope code contributes to the file alone; the start offset is inclusive and the end offset exclusive.

test.name: an_empty_range_index_owns_nothing
test.purpose: A file defining no function attributes nothing, rather than indexing an empty array.

test.name: a_multi_line_statement_counts_once
test.purpose: The same expression written across three lines and on one line yields the same ELOC, so layout cannot move the number.

test.name: only_statements_count_toward_eloc
test.purpose: A directive, a lone brace, a bare declaration, and a blank line contribute nothing, while an initialising declaration and a return each contribute one.

test.name: two_statements_on_one_line_count_once
test.purpose: Two statements sharing a line are one line of code. Counting captures instead would make the same two statements worth twice as much on one line as on two.

test.name: a_nested_functions_statements_are_not_counted_twice
test.purpose: A nested function's statements contribute to it alone, the enclosing function keeps only its own, and the file counts each line once.

test.name: file_scope_code_counts_for_the_file_only
test.purpose: An initialised global contributes to the file's ELOC and to no function's.

test.name: a_file_with_nothing_executable_reports_zero_eloc
test.purpose: A file of comments, directives, and bare declarations reports zero ELOC without error.

test.name: a_trailing_comment_does_not_remove_its_line
test.purpose: A line of code carrying a trailing comment is still a line of code. The exclusion is byte-granular for this reason; a line-granular one deletes the statement.

test.name: a_function_that_never_branches_is_one
test.purpose: A function with no decision point reports 1. A query capturing the function itself would report 2, which is the failure this asserts against.

test.name: each_decision_point_adds_one
test.purpose: Two decision points make three, so the base and the increment are both applied exactly once.

test.name: a_nested_functions_decisions_are_not_counted_twice
test.purpose: A nested named function owns its decision points and the function enclosing it gains none of them; running the query against the enclosing body without attribution would report one more.

test.name: an_unreported_scope_attributes_to_the_named_function_around_it
test.purpose: An offset inside a scope that is not a reported function resolves to the nearest named function containing it. This is the anonymous-callable rule, whose language-level observable waits for a language with lambdas; the mechanism it constrains is verified here.

test.name: a_file_scope_decision_belongs_to_no_function
test.purpose: A conditional in a file-scope initialiser is charged to no function rather than to an arbitrary one.

test.name: filemetrics_free_is_safe_on_null
test.purpose: Releasing a null metrics structure does not fault, so teardown is safe on every path.

test.name: fan_out_counts_distinct_callees
test.purpose: Four call sites to two functions give a fan-out of two, so the measure is of subroutines invoked and not of invocations.

test.name: fan_out_ignores_global_edges
test.purpose: A function that writes a global another reads has a fan-out of zero: coupling through shared state is not invocation.

test.name: direct_recursion_is_detected
test.purpose: A function calling itself is reported as a one-member cycle.

test.name: mutual_recursion_is_detected
test.purpose: A mutually recursive pair is one cycle of two members rather than two cycles of one.

test.name: a_straight_line_program_has_no_cycles
test.purpose: An acyclic call graph reports no recursion, so the trivial single-node components every decomposition produces are not mistaken for self-calls.

test.name: a_global_cycle_is_not_recursion
test.purpose: Two functions each writing a global the other reads form a cycle in the SDG and no recursion at all, which is the case that would otherwise produce a false critical MISRA C Rule 17.2 finding on ordinary code.

test.name: depth_is_the_length_of_the_deepest_chain
test.purpose: A three-function chain from a declared entry point measures three, the entry point counting as the first layer.

test.name: the_deepest_chain_is_an_ordered_sequence
test.purpose: With a shallow branch listed first and a deep one second, the reported chain is the deep one in order — a search taking the first edge would give the wrong path and the wrong length.

test.name: depth_measures_from_the_deepest_entry_point
test.purpose: Given two entry points of different depths, the reported figure and chain are the worst case across them.

test.name: recursion_yields_no_depth_and_terminates
test.purpose: A recursive call graph reports its cycle, no depth figure, and no chain — and the run terminates, which a longest-path search over a cyclic graph would not.

test.name: no_entry_points_omits_depth_with_a_reason
test.purpose: With no declaration the depth analysis is omitted rather than failed, `main` is not inferred despite being present, and the measurements needing no declaration are still produced.

test.name: an_entry_point_matching_nothing_is_a_distinct_omission
test.purpose: A declared entry point naming no analysed function yields a different omission from declaring none, because the two call for different actions.

test.name: depth_carries_the_unresolved_count
test.purpose: The unresolved-call count travels with the depth, since a chain through an unresolved call is not followed and the figure is a lower bound.

test.name: a_chain_does_not_travel_along_a_global_edge
test.purpose: A chain stops at the last function actually called, rather than continuing to one that merely reads a global the callee wrote.

test.name: an_empty_project_measures_nothing_without_failing
test.purpose: A run that analysed nothing produces an empty but valid set of measurements.

test.name: tree_results_free_is_safe_on_null_and_twice
test.purpose: Releasing a null or already-released result set does not fault, so teardown is unconditional on every path.

test.name: excluded_extension_matches_the_runtime_list
test.purpose: An extension present in the runtime list is excluded and one absent from it is not, the list having been read from the runtime location rather than from any table in the binary.

test.name: excluded_extension_ignores_case
test.purpose: One entry covers every spelling of an extension, so a list maintained in lower case still excludes an upper-case file name.

test.name: a_name_without_an_extension_is_not_excluded
test.purpose: A dot occurring in a directory component, and a name that is nothing but a suffix, are both correctly read as having no extension to test.

test.name: an_empty_exclusion_list_excludes_nothing
test.purpose: An empty list excludes nothing, which is the state discovery runs in when the runtime file is absent.

test.name: extension_list_skips_comments_and_blank_lines
test.purpose: Comment and blank lines are not entries, and an entry written without its leading period still matches, so the data file can be maintained in either style.

test.name: a_missing_extension_list_is_not_fatal
test.purpose: An absent binary-extension file yields an empty list rather than aborting the run, so discovery still completes.

test.name: a_regular_file_target_is_appended_directly
test.purpose: A target that is a regular file is appended to the file list with no directory traversal performed for it.

test.name: a_missing_target_is_rejected_with_an_empty_list
test.purpose: A target that does not exist is rejected, and no partial file list survives the rejection.

test.name: a_target_that_is_neither_file_nor_directory_is_rejected
test.purpose: A FIFO named as a target is rejected, covering the class of targets that exist but are neither regular file nor directory.

test.name: every_target_is_validated_before_any_is_walked
test.purpose: A valid target given alongside an invalid one is not walked, so a report can never cover fewer targets than the user named.

test.name: a_file_reached_through_two_targets_appears_once
test.purpose: A file named explicitly and also contained in a named directory is retained once, canonicalisation having preceded de-duplication.

test.name: the_file_list_is_sorted_into_byte_order
test.purpose: The completed list is in ascending byte order whatever order the filesystem enumerated it in.

test.name: hidden_entries_and_binary_extensions_are_excluded
test.purpose: A hidden file, a hidden directory's contents, and a file carrying an excluded extension are all absent from the walk's result.

test.name: the_walk_descends_into_subdirectories
test.purpose: The traversal is recursive: a file several directories below the target is found.

test.name: a_hidden_directory_named_as_the_target_is_traversed
test.purpose: The hidden-entry exclusion applies below the target and not to the target itself, so a hidden directory named on the command line is walked.

test.name: files_and_directories_are_classified_independently
test.purpose: Each target is routed on its own type, so a file and a directory given together are both handled correctly.

test.name: a_cyclic_directory_symlink_terminates
test.purpose: A self-referential directory link does not produce an unbounded traversal, and the linked directory is not descended into. Reaching the assertion is itself the result.

test.name: a_symbolic_link_named_as_a_target_is_resolved
test.purpose: A link named directly as a target is resolved to its referent, the other half of the symbolic-link policy from the one the walk applies.

test.name: a_path_that_cannot_be_canonicalised_is_a_per_file_failure
test.purpose: A canonicalisation failure, provoked through a link-time wrapper, drops that path and records a per-file failure rather than ending the run.

test.name: git_walk_yields_the_tracked_files
test.purpose: The walk enumerates the files committed at `HEAD` and not a file that exists in the working tree but was never added, which is the exclusion the route exists to perform.

test.name: git_walk_is_scoped_to_the_target
test.purpose: Naming a subdirectory enumerates that subdirectory alone, though the tree at `HEAD` is the whole repository.

test.name: git_walk_declines_a_directory_in_no_repository
test.purpose: A directory outside any repository is declined rather than failed: nothing is appended, no failure is recorded, and the negative return is what sends the caller to the filesystem walk.

test.name: git_walk_declines_a_target_the_repository_does_not_track
test.purpose: A directory inside a work tree that `HEAD` knows nothing about — a build directory, or a home directory under version control — is declined, so the target is analysed by traversal instead of reported as empty.

test.name: a_tracked_directory_of_excluded_files_stays_on_the_git_route
test.purpose: A tracked directory whose every tracked file is excluded yields nothing and is still judged applicable, so the run does not fall back and analyse the untracked files beside them. Distinguishes "the repository tracks this directory" from "the repository yielded a file".

test.name: a_route_is_recorded_for_each_target
test.purpose: Each target's route is recorded in the order given, naming the same target twice records it once, and releasing the list leaves it usable rather than stale.

test.name: the_route_list_owns_the_target_it_records
test.purpose: Mutating the caller's buffer after recording does not change the record, so the report can outlive the strings discovery was given.

test.name: filelist_free_is_safe_on_null
test.purpose: Releasing a null file list or extension list does not fault, so teardown is safe on every path.

test.name: every_discovered_function_becomes_a_node
test.purpose: Every function across every analysed file receives a node, so the graph spans the project rather than any one file.

test.name: node_identifiers_follow_sorted_file_order
test.purpose: Files handed over in unsorted order still number their functions by sorted path, so node identifiers are a property of the source tree and not of discovery order.

test.name: a_call_resolves_across_files
test.purpose: A call whose definition lies in another file resolves to an edge, which is the cross-file resolution the graph exists to perform.

test.name: repeated_calls_collapse_to_one_edge_with_a_count
test.purpose: Three call sites between one pair of functions produce one edge carrying a count of three, so out-degree is distinct callees rather than call sites.

test.name: an_unresolvable_call_is_counted_and_does_not_abort
test.purpose: A call into a library is counted, produces no edge, and does not fail the build — no destination is invented for it, which is what keeps a later dead-code proof sound.

test.name: a_call_from_file_scope_has_no_caller_node
test.purpose: A call outside every reported function draws no edge and is counted as unresolved, because the graph does not represent it and the reader is judging completeness.

test.name: a_global_links_its_writer_to_its_reader
test.purpose: A global written in one file and read in another produces an edge between the two functions, and that edge names the object through the graph's own copy of the string.

test.name: an_undeclared_name_is_not_global_state
test.purpose: An identifier written in one function and read in another, declared nowhere at file scope, produces no edge — the over-broad capture is resolved away rather than believed.

test.name: two_objects_between_one_pair_are_two_edges
test.purpose: Global edges are per object and do not collapse the way call edges do, since merging them would lose which shared state couples the two functions.

test.name: an_address_taken_function_is_marked
test.purpose: A function assigned without being called is marked as a reachability root, captured in this phase though Phase 10 is what consumes it.

test.name: an_address_taken_name_that_is_not_a_function_is_discarded
test.purpose: An ordinary variable captured by the deliberately over-broad address-taken patterns resolves to nothing and marks no node, which is what allows the query files not to decide.

test.name: the_component_projection_is_file_level
test.purpose: A call between functions in two files yields one component edge between those files, a component being a source file.

test.name: a_call_within_one_file_is_no_component_dependency
test.purpose: A call inside one file adds no component edge, so a file is not recorded as depending on itself.

test.name: an_empty_project_builds_an_empty_graph
test.purpose: A run that analysed nothing builds a valid empty graph, including the library structure, rather than failing or leaving a null handle.

test.name: the_library_returns_errors_instead_of_aborting
test.purpose: Asking a cyclic graph for a topological ordering returns an error rather than aborting the process, so the library's default abort-on-error handler has been replaced. Reaching the assertion is itself the result: without the handler the test dies rather than fails.

test.name: graph_free_is_safe_on_null_and_twice
test.purpose: Releasing a null or an already-released graph does not fault, so teardown is unconditional on every exit path.

test.name: graphml_is_off_unless_asked_for
test.purpose: With an output path but no request, no export is warranted: the export is opt-in, unlike the .dot companion.

test.name: graphml_needs_an_output_path
test.purpose: With the export requested but the report going to standard output, nothing is warranted — there is no path to derive the companion's name from.

test.name: graphml_is_written_when_asked_for_and_named
test.purpose: Both conditions together warrant the export.

test.name: the_companion_replaces_the_extension
test.purpose: report.md yields report.graphml rather than report.md.graphml: the extension is substituted, not appended.

test.name: a_path_without_an_extension_gains_one
test.purpose: An output path with no extension gains the companion's rather than being left unnamed.

test.name: a_dot_in_a_directory_is_not_an_extension
test.purpose: A dot in a directory name is not mistaken for the file's extension, which would otherwise truncate the path at the directory.

test.name: a_directory_dot_with_an_extension_still_substitutes
test.purpose: A dotted directory alongside a real extension substitutes the extension and leaves the directory alone.

test.name: totals_sum_across_every_file
test.purpose: The project totals are the sum of the per-file physical line counts across every analysed file.

test.name: files_are_presented_in_ascending_path_order
test.purpose: Files are ordered by path in the model, so presentation order is a property of the report rather than of the order the files were discovered.

test.name: an_empty_run_yields_a_complete_model_with_zero_totals
test.purpose: A run in which no file was analysed still produces a complete model with zero totals, which renders normally.

test.name: assembly_leaves_the_accumulator_empty
test.purpose: Ownership of the per-file metrics moves into the report, so releasing both the accumulator and the report cannot free the same metrics twice.

test.name: a_failed_growth_leaves_the_accumulator_intact
test.purpose: A reallocation failure, provoked through a link-time wrapper, is reported and leaves the original allocation intact rather than overwriting it with a null pointer.

test.name: free_is_safe_on_null
test.purpose: Releasing a null report or accumulator does not fault, so teardown is safe on every path.

test.name: the_table_carries_the_summary_and_every_file
test.purpose: The rendered table contains the project summary tier and one row for each file in the model.

test.name: columns_are_aligned_on_the_longest_path
test.purpose: Every file row is rendered to the same width, the path column having been sized from the longest path in the model.

test.name: an_empty_report_still_renders_a_table
test.purpose: A model with no files still renders its headings and column rule, so an empty run is distinguishable from a crash.

test.name: a_write_failure_is_reported
test.purpose: A stream that cannot absorb the report yields a non-zero return, so a truncated report is never reported as success.

test.purpose: A file's language is detected from its extension with no user declaration, and is shown in the report.

test.name: HLR-007: a header is detected as well as a source file
test.purpose: A header maps to a language and its definitions are reported, so a project's headers are not silently uncovered.

test.name: HLR-008: files sharing a language are analysed in one invocation
test.purpose: Several files are analysed in a single invocation and a single pass, with no per-language re-invocation.

test.purpose: Every function discovered is reported with its name and its start and end lines.

test.purpose: Functions appear in start-line order rather than in the order the query happened to match them.

test.name: HLR-012: a file with no language module is listed as skipped

test.name: HLR-012: a skipped file is also reported on stderr
test.purpose: The skip is reported through both observables the requirement names: the list and a diagnostic.

test.name: HLR-037: a skip does not make the exit status non-zero

test.name: HLR-012: a skipped file does not contribute to the totals
test.purpose: A skipped file is accounted for without being counted: the project totals are unchanged by its presence.

test.name: HLR-035: a file that fails to parse does not abort the run
test.purpose: A file that fails to parse leaves the rest of the run intact and the report covers the files that succeeded.

test.name: HLR-120: a parse failure degrades the run to 1
test.purpose: A parse failure produces the status reserved for a run that completed but did not process every file.

test.name: HLR-035: a parse failure names the file on stderr
test.purpose: The diagnostic identifies the file that failed and reaches the diagnostic stream.

test.name: HLR-035: a file with a syntax error is skipped whole, not partially reported

test.name: HLR-019: each file reports its own line and function counts
test.purpose: Each file's row carries its own physical line count and the number of functions it defines.

test.name: HLR-066: a target of only skipped files still reports zero totals

test.name: HLR-025: the totals are broken down by language

test.name: HLR-025: the per-language totals sum to the project totals

test.name: HLR-019: a header of declarations only reports zero ELOC

test.name: an_ordinary_field_is_not_quoted

test.name: a_field_containing_a_comma_is_quoted
test.purpose: A comma is what separates fields, so a value carrying one is quoted — the template-signature case, where one identifier looks like two fields.

test.name: a_quote_is_doubled_not_backslashed
test.purpose: RFC 4180 escapes a quote by doubling it. A backslash escape parses without error and carries the wrong text, which is worse than failing.

test.name: a_field_containing_a_newline_is_quoted
test.purpose: A line break inside a field ends the record unless the field is quoted.

test.name: a_field_containing_a_carriage_return_is_quoted
test.purpose: Records are CRLF-terminated, so a carriage return ends one as surely as a newline.

test.name: a_field_needing_every_escape_survives
test.purpose: A comma, a quote, and a newline in one field are handled together rather than one rule cancelling another.

test.name: an_empty_field_is_emitted_empty

test.name: a_null_field_is_emitted_empty

test.name: the_header_row_is_written

test.name: an_empty_report_is_a_header_alone

test.name: angle_brackets_are_escaped

test.name: quotation_marks_are_escaped

test.name: an_ampersand_in_an_entity_is_escaped_once

test.name: ordinary_text_is_unchanged

test.name: escaping_null_emits_nothing

test.name: the build's required flags survive an overridden CFLAGS
test.purpose: The language standard, the warning set, and the header-dependency generation all appear in the compile command when CFLAGS is overridden from the command line, so a build invoked with an added flag is compiled under the same rules as one invoked with none.

test.name: HLR-041: the build passes no threading flag
test.purpose: The build never passes -pthread, which would silently license a future thread.

test.name: the help block and the real target set agree
test.purpose: Every declared target appears in the makefile's help block and every name in that block is a real target, so the hand-maintained summary cannot drift from what the build actually offers.

test.name: make help prints the block from the file's header
test.purpose: The help target prints the header block itself, marker stripped, so a reader who opens the file and a reader who runs it see one text.

test.name: every grammar is linked with the scanner it requires
test.purpose: No delivered grammar has an unresolved external-scanner symbol. The rule located an optional scanner with a construct make expands before running the recipe, so it looked for a file the fetch above it had not unpacked and silently found none — invisible while C, which has no scanner, was the only grammar.

test.name: the grammar build takes its owner and reference as parameters
test.purpose: The rule for a grammar hosted outside the parsing library's organisation reaches that owner, and fetches by commit rather than by tag because its upstream cuts no releases. Both would be impossible with either value hardcoded.

test.name: every grammar the build declares is one the build can produce
test.purpose: Each name the build lists has a rule behind it. A missing one fails only on a clean tree, which is the tree nobody builds on.

test.name: check-prereqs reports every grammar against upstream
test.purpose: Each delivered language appears in the dependency report, so a pin that is immutable is not thereby invisible when it falls behind.

test.name: check-prereqs survives an unreachable upstream
test.purpose: An unreachable upstream reports "unknown" rather than failing or hanging: the report is a diagnostic a person runs, not a gate.

test.name: every runtime data file the build does not produce is tracked
test.purpose: Every file under the runtime location that the build does not itself produce is tracked by the repository, so that a version-control ignore rule cannot silently exclude product data. `.gitignore` carries `*.map` for linker map files, which also matched the extension table: it worked locally, was absent from the clone CI made, and every parsing test then failed naming the missing file rather than the rule that hid it.

test.name: HLR-043: elc does not modify the tree it analyses
test.purpose: The analysed tree checksums identically before and after a run.

test.name: HLR-043: elc opens nothing for writing
test.purpose: No syscall capable of modifying a file — an open carrying a writing mode, a creat, an unlink, a truncate, or a rename — is observed for the whole run. This is direct evidence of read-only operation, where comparing checksums afterwards is only circumstantial.

test.name: HLR-076: each source file is opened exactly once
test.purpose: No source file is opened twice for the whole run, which is the observable form of the single-parse rule: a second open would mean some stage re-read it.

test.name: HLR-009: the grammar is loaded from the runtime location, not linked
test.purpose: No grammar appears among the binary's link-time dependencies, and the grammar file is opened during the run — language support is loaded at run time rather than compiled in.

test.name: HLR-043: elc runs against a read-only directory
test.purpose: A run succeeds against a directory with write permission removed.

test.name: the fixture level is wired and elc is runnable
test.purpose: The fixture-conformance level is wired and green before the first real fixture is written.

test.name: every expected-value file has a fixture header beside it
test.purpose: Guards the convention that expected values are hand-counted, never generated from elc's own output.
